**date: 2026-10-29**

**US Pre-Market Brief — Thursday, 29 October 2026**

- **Mode: WEEKDAY.** The last completed US cash session was **Wednesday 28 October 2026**. All "close / %chg" columns below are that Wednesday session.
- All "pre-market" columns are live prints taken between 08:35 and 09:05 ET on Thursday 29 October, before the 09:30 ET open.
- The 08:30 ET BEA release (Q3 advance GDP + September PCE) landed ~25 minutes into this run's snapshot window, so the pre-market gaps already partly reflect it —
- but the screen-level quotes were pulled in two waves and should be read as **pre-open indications, not settled**.

---

**1. TL;DR — theme first**

- **The AI-capex trade is being re-priced off a single print, and the re-pricing is violent.**
- Alphabet reported after Wednesday's close and is **−11.1% pre-market** ($288.69) on a revenue miss, a $9.07B negative free-cash-flow quarter and 2027 capex guidance that will "increase significantly." GOOGL −11.2% ($285.83), and the sympathy damage spreads across the entire AI-infrastructure complex that rallied Wednesday:
- **NBIS −7.4%, CRWV −7.2%, AXTI −7.4%, IREN −5.4%, WULF −4.4%, GLXY −5.2%, VRT −3.8%, FLEX −4.6%, CLS −3.3%, SNDK −3.0%, AAOI −2.9%**.
- Read this as a *funding-cost* repricing of AI capex, not an earnings-season glitch.

- **The market is paying only for accelerating growth.** Three names that beat on the headline
- and were sold anyway: **FTNT −26.9%** ($127.16;
- beat on EPS and revenue, raised full-year revenue guidance, then cut service-revenue guidance and decelerated total growth from 26% to 20%), **NOW −18.9%** ($121.80;
- Q3 miss plus a softer contracted-revenue outlook), and **XRX −31.2%** ($1.92;
- EPS beat of $0.02 vs −$0.10 expected, but FY26 adjusted operating income guidance cut to $450–475M from $555–605M and free-cash-flow guidance cut to $50–100M from $250M).
- In each case the *guidance shape*, not the quarter, was the problem.

- **Iovance (−31%) is the cautionary tale of a good print.** IOVA's 08:00 ET release showed
- Phase 2 IOV-LUN-202 overall response rate of **24.6% (17/69)** — consistent with the prior 25.6% —
- but the headline 59.1% ORR lives in a 22-patient KRAS-wild-type/HER2-wild-type/ ever-smoker subgroup, while the KRAS-mutant subgroup responded at only **11.4% (4/35)**.
- With the sBLA pushed to 2027, the stock gave back a ~440% YTD run and an after-hours Wednesday rally.
- It is the #1 name on StockTwits and the single worst pre-market gap on the screen.

- **Freight is a cost story, not a demand story — and it bounced today.** Wednesday's
- transport rout was about cost inflation: **LSTR −17.8%** (EPS $1.42 vs $1.67 expected;
- insurance and claims $55.3M vs $33.0M a year ago), ODFL −7.3% *despite* beating, CHRW −11.1%, WERN −7.7%, RXO −5.2%.
- This morning **SAIA reported a record $982.5M revenue (+17.0%) and $3.41 diluted EPS** (consensus ~$3.31) but with a deteriorated 87.6% operating ratio, and the group is green:
- SAIA +2.6%, ODFL +1.2%, CHRW +0.5%.

- **Rotation is running hard away from tech and into defensives and quality.** Pre-market
- sector ETFs: **XLV +2.26%, XLP +1.52%, XLF +1.34%, XLU +1.08%, XLRE +1.04%, XLE +0.98%, XLY +0.85%** against **XLK −1.46% and XLC −1.78%**.
- The single-name version of the same trade: **LLY +5.1%, NCLH +12.4%, MA +3.2%, MRK +2.4%, GILD +3.4%, MSFT +1.2%**.

- **Crypto-equity is breaking while spot barely moves.** BTC $80,092 (−0.87% 24h), ETH $2,323.42
- (−0.86%), but the listed proxies are down 2.8–5.2%: **MARA −4.1%, RIOT −3.9%, CLSK −3.6%, MSTR −3.1%, COIN −2.8%, GLXY −5.2%**.
- Equity beta is amplifying a flat tape — and COIN and MSTR both report today.

- **Macro: strong growth, benign quarter-on-quarter inflation, in-line monthly inflation.**
- BEA's 08:30 ET advance estimate put **Q3 real GDP at +3.4%** (consensus 3.2%, Atlanta Fed GDPNow 3.27%) but the **Q3 PCE price index at only 2.1%** (core 2.5%, Q2:
- 5.0% / 3.3%). September PCE printed **+0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y** — in line with consensus.
- Personal income +0.2% (below the +0.3% estimate); nominal spending +0.5%; **real PCE spending +0.0%**, a sharp slowdown from +0.5%.
- The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on Wednesday in a **10–2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25bp hike** ,
- so this is a growth-beat / inflation-in-line mix that argues against a December hike.

**2. Theme clusters**

**Cluster A — Alphabet's negative FCF re-rates the entire AI-capex complex**

- **Leader:** GOOGL, **−11.1% pre-market** ($288.69; last print $287.90, −11.39%). GOOG
−11.2% ($285.83). Wednesday close $324.89 (+1.34%).

- **What broke:** Q3 revenue $127.58B vs $128.22B expected (+25% y/y); adjusted EPS $2.67 vs
- $3.02 expected; GAAP EPS $2.12 on an $8.7B equity-securities loss; **free cash flow −$9.07B** (first negative in 22 years as a public company) against expectations of roughly break-even;
- advertising revenue $82.01B, $1.41B below consensus; Search +12% to $63.35B vs $64.96B expected; YouTube ads $11.2B vs $11.4B expected. Operating income $40.58B vs $43.19B expected.
- Q3 capex $51.36B *under* the ~$55.09B expected — which is the part that hurt: hyperscaler capex came in light, raising questions about near-term AI hardware order pace.
- FY26 capex guidance held at $195–205B, with CFO Anat Ashkenazi saying 2027 capex will "increase significantly."

- **Corroborators (the complex giving back Wednesday's gains):** NBIS −7.4% ($168.93),
- CRWV −7.2% ($59.32), AXTI −7.4% ($59.62), IREN −5.4% ($27.28), WULF −4.4% ($12.83), VRT −3.8% ($233.75), FLEX −4.6% ($88.78), CLS −3.3% ($290.00), SNDK −3.0% ($1,362.32), AAOI −2.9% ($79.84).
- All of these *rallied* on Wednesday — VRT +16.5%, FLEX +11.6%, CLS +8.4%, SNDK +7.7%, NBIS +7.0%, CRWV +7.3%, IREN +5.1% — and are giving it back.

- **Counterpoint that keeps this a rotation and not a crash:** MSFT is **+1.2%** pre-market
- ($537.51) after Azure accelerated to 48%, and ORCL is only **−1.9%** ($141.80) after its Wednesday +10.7% investor-day rally on a path to positive free cash flow.
- Oracle and Microsoft were rewarded for their capex financing; Alphabet was not.

- **News:** https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-googl-earnings-q3-2026.html ·
https://www.reuters.com/business/alphabets-google-cloud-unit-beats-quarterly-revenue-estimates-steady-ai-demand-2026-10-28/

**Cluster B — "Beat and still get sold": guidance shape is the whole story**

- **FTNT −26.9%** ($127.16 pre-market; last $125.99, −27.6%). Q3 revenue $2.08B (+20%) vs
- $2.06B expected; non-GAAP EPS $0.91 vs $0.86; billings $2.34B (+29%); full-year revenue guidance raised a third time to $8.125–8.215B. The sell-off drivers: revenue growth decelerated from 26% to 20%;
- **service-revenue guidance cut to $5.15–5.17B from $5.18–5.22B**; non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 79.6% from 81.6%; the CFO called it "really a timing issue." Buyback authorisation raised $1.2B, $2B left.
- Sympathy: **PANW −6.7%** ($368.00), **ZS −7.1%** ($237.53) — neither reported anything.

- **NOW −18.9%** ($121.80; 1.71M pre-market shares). Q3 earnings miss and a softer outlook for
contracted-revenue growth, overshadowing revenue growth and raised AI targets.

- **XRX −31.2%** ($1.92; 520k pre-market shares) — reported Thursday morning. Q3 revenue $1.868B
- (−4.7% y/y, in line with $1.86B consensus), adjusted EPS $0.02 vs −$0.10 expected, adjusted operating income $124M vs $65M y/y —
- but a **$955M goodwill impairment** drove a $1.019B net loss ($−7.73/share), and FY26 adjusted operating income guidance was cut to $450–475M from $555–605M with FCF guidance cut to ~$50–100M from $250M.
- It also refinanced ~$174M of 2028 notes into 2030 first-lien paper plus stock (~$53M principal reduction). Debt-to-equity above 700% makes it the most rate-sensitive name on the board.

- **MRVL −11.9%** ($221.63; 1.91M pre-market shares) — reports of advanced talks to acquire
Lumentum; the market is debating strategic value against financing, dilution and integration risk. No deal confirmed.

- **News:** https://investor.fortinet.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fortinet-reports-strong-third-quarter-2026-financial-results ·
https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/first-f5-now-fortinet-wall-street-has-stopped-paying-security-stocks-for-beating-earnings/ · https://www.rttnews.com/3705350/xerox-q3-loss-widens-cuts-fy26-adj-income-view-backs-revenue-outlook-stock-down-22.aspx

**Cluster C — Biotech: a good dataset that narrows the market**

- **Leader: IOVA −31.3%** pre-market ($10.18 on TradingView, $10.10 on Nasdaq; last print
$10.37, −29.95%; 5.7–7.8M pre-market shares). Wednesday close $14.81 (+1.58%).

- **The data (8:00 ET release, 8:30 ET webcast):** 69 patients in IOV-LUN-202 Cohorts 1–2,
- **ORR 24.6% (17/69)** — "consistent with previously reported" 25.6%.
- The dramatic number is real but narrow: a retrospective biomarker-enriched subgroup of **22 patients** (KRAS wild-type + HER2 wild-type + current/former smoker) produced **13 of the 17 responses, 59.1% ORR**.
- The KRAS-mutant subgroup was **11.4% (4/35)**; KRAS wild-type overall 43.3% (13/30).
- Cohorts are completing enrolment at ~80 patients, sBLA targeted for 2027, and a new registrational-intent study (POSITIVITY) begins enrolling November 2026.
- The stock was up ~12% Wednesday night and near its 52-week high of $15.37 before the detail printed.

- **Read:** the market repriced the *breadth* of the opportunity, not the efficacy. This is a
single-name idiosyncratic event with a live 8:30 ET webcast still in progress at snapshot time and Q3 earnings on 5 November.

- **The biotech tape around it:** XLV is the best pre-market sector at **+2.26%**, while the
Wednesday biotech winners faded — REPL −0.9%, SLS −1.3%, BEAM −3.6%, SDGR −4.4%, AXGN +0.7%, ALMR −2.0%, DNA −2.4%.

- **News:** https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/iovance-reports-updated-iov-lun-110000935.html ·
https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/iovance-stock-falls-lung-cancer-114613763.html

**Cluster D — Freight/transport: insurance, diesel and compensation**

- Wednesday's rout was cost-driven. **LSTR −17.8%** (Wednesday): EPS $1.42 vs $1.67 expected on
- revenue $1.512B (+25.4%); insurance and claims cost **$55.3M vs $33.0M** a year earlier (~$13M adverse reserve development plus ~$8M for two accident claims); gross margin fell to 8.4% from 9.2%.
- Truist cut its target to $160, JPM to $172. Management framed it as a bumpy patch in a tightening market, with October revenue per load ~+29% y/y.

- **ODFL −7.3%** on Wednesday *despite* beating ($1.65 vs $1.61; revenue $1.59B) — the clearest
evidence that cost, not demand, is driving the group.

- **CHRW −11.1%, WERN −7.7%, RXO −5.2%, SNDR −4.5%, HCC −4.5%, SAIA −4.8%** on Wednesday, with
diesel near $6.28/gal and 16 US trucking bankruptcies filed in the month as backdrop.

- **This morning SAIA reported before the open:** revenue a record **$982.5M (+17.0%)**,
- LTL tonnage per workday a record (+8.9%), diluted EPS **$3.41** vs $3.22 a year ago (consensus ~$3.31) — but operating ratio **87.6% vs 85.9%** adjusted a year ago.
- SAIA is **+2.6%** pre-market ($333.00) on thin volume (284 shares), ODFL +1.2% ($175.34), CHRW +0.5% ($128.19). The cost story is capping the bounce.

- **News:** https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/saia-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-1036684558 ·
https://www.charlotteobserver.com/news/business/article317822222.html · https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/old-dominion-freight-line-odfl-113505518.html

**Cluster F — Crypto-equity decoupling from spot**

- **Spot barely moved:** BTC **$80,092** (−0.87% 24h), ETH **$2,323.42** (−0.86% 24h).
- **Listed proxies did not:** MARA −4.1% ($7.05), RIOT −3.9% ($13.89), CLSK −3.6% ($8.27),
- MSTR −3.1% ($140.60), COIN −2.8% ($157.67), GLXY −5.2% ($18.13) — i.e.
- roughly a 3–5× amplification of the spot move, in the same direction, while every one of them rallied Wednesday (MSTR +2.7%, COIN +0.8%, MARA +3.7%, RIOT +6.6%, CLSK +4.8%).
- Classic beta unwind.

- **Both COIN and MSTR are scheduled to report today** (TradingView earnings calendar), so the
complex carries event risk into the close.

- Note: GLXY's Wednesday rally was crypto-driven (+11.1%) and it is now giving back 5.2%.
